chunks: Saʿīd ibn Yasār asked him about exchanging one camel for two camels, hand to hand or on credit, and he said:
Yes, there is no harm if the ages are specified, whether they are jadhaʿān or thaniyyān.
Then he instructed me, so I struck out the mention of credit, because the people say no; and he only did that for taqiyyah.

key_terms.الْأَسْنَانُ: the ages or age categories of the animals
key_terms.الْبَعِيرِ: a camel used here as the commodity being exchanged
key_terms.ثَنِيَّانَ: two animals of a specified more mature age category
key_terms.جَذَعَانَ: two animals of a specified younger age category
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no legal objection or harm
key_terms.لِلتَّقِيَّةِ: for taqiyyah, precautionary dissimulation under circumstances of risk

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to exchange one camel for two camels, including on credit, in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on exchanging camels in unequal numbers, indicating permissibility when the animals’ ages are clearly specified. It also records that the mention of deferred exchange was struck out due to taqiyyah, reflecting the social and juristic pressures surrounding such rulings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4010 - Sa'id ibn Yasar asked him about exchanging one camel for two camels, whether hand-to-hand or on credit.
Imam (as) said: "Yes, there is no harm if their ages are specified, whether they are young or mature."
Then Imam (as) instructed me to strike out the mention of credit because people say it is not allowed, and Imam (as) only did that as a precaution (taqiyyah).
